messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] reserved-pool-resv-nyc-1 at 100% GPU utilization; queue length=432; autoscaler error=ScaleGroupLimitExceeded; severity=P2. Paging @oncall and @eng-sre :rotating_light:
Sam (oncall): Got the page, I'm on it. What customers are impacted?
Leah (customer-success): I'm seeing high errors from Enterprise: 'HalcyonHealth' & 'StellarPay' on our status page. Both are on reserved pools in nyc. Customers alerted in their incident channels; setting expectation that we're investigating.
Priya (eng-sre): Checking autoscaler logs now. Running: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed list-instances resv-nyc-1` — hang on.
Priya (eng-sre): Autoscaler kept trying to add nodes but got repeated 403s from cloud API with body: `{"error":"ScaleGroupLimitExceeded","message":"quota reached for GPU quota (v100) in region us-east1"}`. Looks like we hit a quota/soft-limit at provider.
Jorge (runtime): That matches runtime metrics: continuous batching backlog increasing, workers at 100% GPU mem, KV cache thrash. We have ~430 pending requests in queue across the resv pool.
Sam (oncall): Can we failover those tenants to fallback region or fallback model variant? What's the risk to SLAs?
Jorge (runtime): We support automatic fallback to compatible variant in us-west-2; but reserved tenants have policy to prefer pinned region. We can temporarily route traffic to a compatible variant (smaller model) in us-west-2 with degraded latency but should keep throughput. Requires manual policy flip for the two enterprise tenants.
Priya (eng-sre): Two immediate mitigations: 1) Evict best-effort / non-enterprise sessions from resv-nyc-1 (noisy neighbors), 2) Open a temporary route for HalcyonHealth+StellarPay to us-west-2 fallback models. Implementing 1 now: `resvctl evict-sessions --pool resv-nyc-1 --filter "tenant!=enterprise" --dry-run=false`
infra-bot: command accepted; evicting 128 sessions over next 60s; estimated freed GPUs per node: ~0.4.
Jorge (runtime): Eviction in progress, seeing slight drop in local queue, but still ~320 pending. The noisy sessions looked like a long-running batch job from tenant 'greenfield-ads' using large context lengths.
Sam (oncall): Leah, can you notify HalcyonHealth/StellarPay that we're initiating a failover and may see higher latency for ~30-45m?
Leah (customer-success): Notifying now. Adding escalation contact for HalcyonHealth (ops@halcyon). I'll post updates in their bridge.
Emma (product): When you flip routing, remember cost impact — routing to fallback will increase token cost ~1.6x. Flag internal billing.
Priya (eng-sre): Preparing routing change: `routingctl set-policy --tenant halcyonhealth --pool resv-nyc-1 --fallback us-west-2-compat --force --reason "autoscale quota hit"`
infra-bot: routing policy change queued; applying to halcyonhealth and stellarpay.
Priya (eng-sre): Applied for HalcyonHealth. Applied for StellarPay. Confirming connection handshakes to us-west-2.
Jorge (runtime): New requests for both tenants are hitting us-west-2. Observed initial successful handshakes. Latency increased ~220ms median, but requests flowing. Queue on resv-nyc-1 down to 90.
Sam (oncall): Good. Remaining backlog on resv-nyc-1 is largely internal CI and retry storms. Any way to throttle retries or apply short-term token bucket?
Priya (eng-sre): We can enable aggressive per-tenant rate limiting for non-enterprise: `ratelimitctl set --pool resv-nyc-1 --policy aggressive-temp --duration 20m` — doing it now.
infra-bot: ratelimit policy applied; observed rate of incoming sessions decreased by ~48% within 30s.
Jorge (runtime): Queue now at ~24 pending, GPU utilization falling to ~72% across nodes. Autoscaler still blocked until quota resolved but traffic is manageable.
Sam (oncall): Who owns cloud quota requests? Can we fast-track an increase?
Priya (eng-sre): Ops to contact cloud-quotas team. Pinged cloud-support ticket #CLOUD-98765 and requested emergency quota bump for v100 in us-east1. ETA unknown but asked for immediate review.
Leah (customer-success): HalcyonHealth replied — thanks, they accept redirect to fallback for now. StellarPay asked for an interim SLA credit; I'll open a ticket with account team.
Emma (product): Let's capture this as a short post-incident note: noisy neighbor + provider quota = reserved pool outage. Recommend we: 1) add proactive quota monitoring and alerting, 2) auto-fallback for enterprise tenants after X minutes, 3) classify long-running batch jobs and surface to support before they take nodes.
Sam (oncall): Agreed. For now I'll mark this incident as 'mitigated' once queue < 10 and enterprise tenants in fallback are stable. Keeping channel open for postmortem details.
Priya (eng-sre): Queue steady at 6. GPUs at ~58%. Autoscaler still showing ScaleGroupLimitExceeded in logs but that's less urgent now.
Jorge (runtime): I'll follow up with a quick patch to runtime to detect noisy long-context sessions and surface them into a 'scheduling' bucket to avoid eviction cold starts.
infra-bot: Cloud support replied: ticket COLD-98765 triaged; pending quota change — could take 4-6 hours.
Sam (oncall): Noted. We'll keep fallback in place until quota resolved and add a follow-up runbook. Closing primary pager, leaving monitoring watch for 2 hours. 
Leah (customer-success): Closing customer bridges with status updates. HalcyonHealth/ StellarPay on incident watch.
Emma (product): I'll create the action items doc and assign owners. Good job team. :tada:
